strings: Fraggar Thundermantle, a Wildhammer, has already taken troll tribal necklaces from you once under this bounty. The offer stands for more, as long as you bring them five at a time.

Fraggar reminds you the first handing-over is behind you, yet more troll tribal necklaces are still welcome whenever you find them and choose to hand them over. First Mate Fitzsimmons, the sole living survivor of the Third Fleet of Kul Tiras, asks for mercy on behalf of his lost brethren. Trapped by a dark relic hidden aboard their sunken ships off the Wetlands coast, the drowned sailors and marines wander the wrecks as restless undead.

When the Third Fleet of Kul Tiras foundered along the jagged shores north of Menethil Harbor, its tragedy did not end beneath the waves. While First Mate Fitzsimmons managed to wash ashore alive, his fellow crewmen met a fate far worse than death. A mysterious and terrible treasure hidden deep within one of the hulls unleashed an eerie sorcery upon the dying sailors, binding their souls to the sea-battered timbers and denying them the peace of the grave.

Fitzsimmons, lingering in the taverns of Menethil Harbor, remains haunted by the nightly moans and cries of his former shipmates. Believing that putting down their animated corpses will offer them release, he sends adventurers into the rotting, drowned hulks to strike down the cursed sailors, the seasoned marines, and his former peer, First Mate Snellig, retrieving Snellig's personal snuffbox as grim proof that his friend has finally been laid to rest.

First Mate Snellig served aboard the ill-fated Third Fleet of Kul Tiras alongside First Mate Fitzsimmons. After the fleet wrecked off the northern coast of the Wetlands, Snellig drowned with the rest of the crew, only to be resurrected by the malevolent relic stowed aboard the ships. He now haunts the flooded hold of one of the wrecks as an undead horror.

Striking down the sailors and marines grants temporary respite to their restless spirits, but it does not shatter the enchantment entirely. The root of the curse remains tied to the mysterious relic still hidden aboard the wreckage.

The Trial of the Lake is a timed challenge held in Moonglade that tests an initiate's physical dexterity and speed. Aspirants must dive into Lake Elune'ara to retrieve an unstable Shrine Bauble and rush it to the Shrine of Remulos before it decays. Successful completion earns recognition from the warden Tajarri and honors the Cenarion Circle's dedication to balance.

The Trial of the Lake is an introductory rite overseen by the guardians of Moonglade. Aspirants are charged with diving into the tranquil waters of Lake Elune'ara to recover a delicate Shrine Bauble resting along the sunken lakebed. Because the bauble rapidly decays once disturbed from its resting place, the trial demands sharp physical dexterity, keen senses, and swift movement to carry it overland before its magic fades.

Upon securing the bauble, runners must hurry to the Shrine of Remulos in northwestern Moonglade. The monument stands as a lasting tribute to Keeper Remulos, who guides the Cenarion Circle in the preservation of nature and world balance. Activating the bauble at the shrine serves as a ceremonial nod to its significance within the Circle. There, the trusted warden Tajarri greets initiates who successfully overcome the trial's time limit and competition.

The Trial of the Lake is a test of agility and focus set in Moonglade. Initiates dive into the cold depths of Lake Elune'ara to retrieve a decaying Shrine Bauble, rushing it across the haven to the Shrine of Remulos before its energy dissipates.

First Mate Fitzsimmons believes that the restless curse binding his fallen crewmates stems from a dark artifact secured aboard their wrecked ship, the Intrepid. To set his brethren free, an adventurer must face the ghost of Captain Halyndor, take the strongbox key, and recover the relic from the submerged hull.

First Mate Fitzsimmons survived the tragic fate of the Third Fleet, but the memory of his comrades haunts his waking hours and his dreams. He remains convinced that the undeath gripping his shipmates is tied to a mysterious, malignant object locked away inside the strongbox of his old vessel, the Intrepid. Overseeing the wreck is the spectral remnants of Captain Halyndor, who even in death fiercely guards the key to the vessel's deepest secrets.

Off the mist-choked coast of the northern Wetlands lie the fractured hulks of the Third Fleet. Resting within the flooded hull of the Intrepid, the ship's locked strongbox holds the relic at the heart of the crew's misery. Reclaiming it requires defeating Halyndor's tortured ghost on deck, securing the rusted key, and braving the flooded interior to retrieve the dark artifact so that holy hands can cleanse it.

Hadoken Swiftstrider is sure the Woodpaw gnolls follow some written strategy. He sends you to search the gnoll camps south of Camp Mojache for anything resembling battle plans.

This comes after Alpha Strike. Hadoken has little respect for gnoll brains, yet he is sure they keep some record of their strategy, as their recent assaults are too well coordinated to be improvised. If he could see those plans, he would better understand what stirred them up. He sends you back to the Woodpaw to find whatever looks like battle plans and bring it to him.

The map is indeed what Hadoken wanted. Arrows cross it that might show troop movements, but most run south, away from Camp Mojache in the north. Elsewhere on the map is a drawing of what you take to be a big insect, with tick marks beneath it, maybe a count of the gnolls' losses to unknown bugs.

Senir Whitebeard sends an urgent report from Kharanos to Senator Barin Redstone in Ironforge. He warns that the senator is sour and asks you to keep the scout who gathered the information unnamed.

Senir Whitebeard needs you to carry an urgent report from Kharanos to Senator Barin Redstone in Ironforge. The mountaineer’s account details the growing Frostmane troll threat facing Dun Morogh, drawn from reconnaissance deep inside Frostmane Hold. Senir asks you not to mention who helped gather the information from the snowy crags.

Senator Barin Redstone reacts with anger when you deliver Senir’s report in Ironforge’s royal court. The senator bristles at the report’s use of King Magni’s authority to sanction Senir’s operations. His response reveals resentment in the Senate toward the King’s decrees and field initiatives carried out in his name.

This quest sees an adventurer recover a blackened, pulsating gem known as the Cursed Eye of Paleth from the flooded wreckage of the Intrepid. Recovered at the behest of the haunted sailor Fitzsimmons, the malevolent artifact must be brought to Menethil Harbor so the dwarven priest Glorin Steelbrow can divine how to purge its blight.

Beneath the treacherous waters of the Baradin Bay, resting inside the locked strongbox of the sunken vessel Intrepid, lies no ordinary treasure. The chest yields a blackened orb pulsing with an unsettling radiance: an Eye of Paleth. Rather than gleaning sacred light, this particular stone has been warped into an engine of suffering, heavily tied to the restless spirits and doom that claimed the sailors of the Third Fleet.

Recognizing that such dark magic exceeds common salvage, the artifact is brought directly ashore to Menethil Harbor. There, Glorin Steelbrow, a dwarven priest of the Holy Light, inspects the anomaly. While stunned that such a sacred device was ever in the possession of the Third Fleet, Glorin immediately recognizes its unnatural taint and begins preparing the rites necessary to undo its dark influence.

The Eye of Paleth is an ancient and powerful sacred gem. Normally associated with holy energies, this particular specimen was aboard the sunken Third Fleet vessel Intrepid and has become twisted and cursed, radiating dark magic.

Tinkmaster Overspark sends Alliance adventurers into Gnomeregan for Techbot's memory core. The machine once aided researchers, but radiation and an electrical surge during the city's fall left its brain polarized and its behavior violent. Overspark hopes the core will help him reverse the damage and restore his creation.

Before Gnomeregan fell, Techbot aided researchers with its many devices and vast technical knowledge. Tinkmaster Overspark designed the mechanical assistant, whose integrated gizmos made it a marvel of gnomish ingenuity. The trogg invasion brought chaos, and toxic radiation filled the city. A stray electrical surge jolted Techbot's delicate inner workings, polarizing its positronic brain into a volatile negatronic state.

Techbot now wanders Gnomeregan's contaminated halls in a frenzy, attacking anyone in sight. Overspark refuses to abandon his prized assistant as scrap. He asks capable operatives to find the machine, remove its memory core from the metal chassis, and bring it to Ironforge. With the core, the Tinkmaster hopes to understand the polarization and repair Techbot's mind.

The Plates of Uldum are discs made by the Creators that store data on their activities at Uldum. They are almost the same size as your own discs, but their markings concern Uldum rather than Uldaman. Uldum is a research facility, where the Creators work to enhance Azeroth's biosphere, and details of their work are for those who hold the Plates. In the end the Watcher promises that your discs will be returned once you access the pedestal, and that you may enter the complex once you have the Plates in your set.

The Stone Watcher adds that the Creators control the distribution of these discs for all the complexes of this world, and that Azeroth has been rescheduled for a visitation. The Creators use visitation to reestablish control over seeded worlds whenever forces from outside or within upset the balance of those worlds' matrix dynamics, and it is not to be taken lightly.
